extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs; Department of the Interior; Congress; Indian agents and agency administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical recommendations for administering Indian agencies as expressed in an 1880 United States Indian Agent annual report: operations, buildings, schools, police, public health, land policy, and legal/administrative actions. Useful for preparing or evaluating agency reports and policy recommendations to the Department of the Interior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of Texas cattle on reservations / stock raising
rubrics_metrics.description: The department has decided to prevent the driving of Texas cattle on the reservation; stock raising will increase now that such driving is prevented and, as the range is fine and extensive, it must necessarily prove very profitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preventing outside droves (Texas cattle) from using reservation range protects and encourages local stock-raising and will make it more profitable for Indians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renting privilege to encourage farm improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whites rent and improve farms for one-third of the crops for a term of years; many Indians have good farms now who, if this privilege had been denied them, would probably never have owned any improvements more than the proverbial 'truck patch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow regulated renting to enable farm improvements and independent support for destitute Indians, while recognizing the renting privilege may be abused and such abuses are often the agent's fault; agents should supervise to prevent exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to employ saw-mill for cheap lumber
rubrics_metrics.description: More substantial improvements would be made if the department would allow us to employ a saw-mill to make lumber for all the tribes. This is the only way to get cheap lumber, and, if permitted, I am sure next year would show a decided increase that would justify the experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizing and supporting local saw-mill operation lowers construction costs and facilitates building houses and improvements that would otherwise be 'up-hill' with rough logs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and repair of agency buildings and employee residences
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent's residence and the commissary are the only buildings of any value here. There is a pressing need for residences for the other employes. Both the Seneca and Quapaw missions must be thoroughly repaired, and bath-houses, as a sanitary measure, should be erected at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize building and repairing residences, mission buildings, and school additions; money spent on such infrastructure is highly effective ('will return, in the good it does, a thousand fold').

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize education as a cost-effective policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Past experience goes far to prove that it is cheaper to educate our wards than make war on them, or let them grow up in ignorance. Ignorance, superstition, degradation, and poverty go hand in hand; intelligence, thrift, industry, and riches follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in schools (day and boarding), accommodate more pupils, and expand educational opportunities as a primary tool for civilization and long-term savings versus coercive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support manual-labor and day schools with vocational training
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual-labor schools teach sewing, laundry, dining-room and kitchen work for girls, and all the branches of agriculture for boys; farms attached to schools supply crops and work experience. Boarding-school additions are needed to accommodate more scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and expand manual-labor boarding-schools and day schools, provide vocational instruction and farm work, and use school farms to support the institution and teach practical skills; send worthy pupils to institutions like Hampton and Carlisle for further education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an effective police force with sufficient pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Our police force was so badly crippled by Congress at its last session that its usefulness is well-nigh destroyed. No one who knows anything about the necessity for such a force will doubt ... when you offer no more inducement to the very best young men we have than $5 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure police are properly paid and equipped; fair compensation is essential to retain capable men and to provide indispensable law-and-order functions until superior judicial arrangements exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress unlawful whisky traffic and punish traffickers severely
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts have been and are being made to suppress this unlawful traffic. Three parties were convicted and fined, and other cases are now pending. I hope by persistent watchfulness to break up the business. A term in the penitentiary for a few of the guilty parties would do more good than anything else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use persistent surveillance, prosecutions, and imprisonment (including penitentiary terms) to deter and break up liquor smuggling and retailing that fuels crime and drunkenness among Indians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and facilitate missionary and temperance work
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been preaching nearly every Sunday and a Sabbath school is successfully conducted ... They have a flourishing temperance organization; each tribe is visited and meetings are held by different ministers from Kansas and Missouri from week to week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support missionary presence and temperance organizations, and encourage more committed missionaries to work among the tribes rather than directing resources abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote allotment / individual homesteads for heads of families
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotment would encourage and advance them in civilization. Each head of a family should have a homestead; let them know that this is their home forever; encourage them in their labors for independence; in other words, make them freemen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor allotment policies that give individual land titles/homesteads to heads of families to incentivize independent agriculture and investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate transportation and warehousing for Indian supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: During the past year the Indians have transported with their own teams ... 35,550 pounds of government's freight ... Our supplies arriving at a season of the year when Indians are busily engaged in haying, it is difficult to procure teams ... There being no warehouse for storing the supplies, we were compelled to use two small, old, dilapidated log cabins for store-rooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund and build proper warehouses and plan logistics to avoid depending on Indians to freight government supplies at critical agricultural times; authorized construction (example: 100 by 20 feet warehouse) and modest appropriations can remedy storage and delay issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep saw-mill running and repair agency industrial equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: We have also a steam saw-mill in running order, but needing some repairs. We have sawed the past year 70,000 feet of lumber and 26,000 shingles for the Indians and government work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and repair industrial equipment (sawmills, etc.) because they produce tangible outputs (lumber/shingles) that support construction and agency needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erect sanitary infrastructure and address water quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Bath-houses, as a sanitary measure, should be erected at once. Owing to the failure of springs, caused by the drought, many families were compelled to use stagnant water from pools; this was the occasion of some sickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in sanitary facilities (bath-houses) and ensure safe water supplies and medical care to control malarious-type diseases and reduce exposure-related illness among Indians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent's judicial role and appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: This agency differs ... Each of these tribes has executive, legislative, and judicial branches of government ... The duties of the agent, with the exception of the payment of annuities ... are of a judicial character. There is no court with jurisdiction to try cases when an Indian is one party and a citizen of the United States or corporation is the other, so the agent is compelled to act as arbitrator. ... subject to an appeal to the Hon. Commissioner of Indian Affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that agents must adjudicate disputes in the absence of U.S. courts, apply fair arbitration practices, and allow appeals to the Commissioner for large or contested cases; consider the need for establishing proper courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and remove intruders without tribal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: As near as can be estimated, there are 6,000 citizens of the United States living within the limits of this agency who have no rights whatever. The authorities have reported to me such as are very troublesome, and they have been removed from the country. ... steps are now being taken to ascertain their names and location, with a view to report and demand the action of the government as the treaty provides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically identify non-rights-holding intruders, document their presence, and request federal action under treaty provisions to remove unsuitable settlers from Indian lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal or revise law prohibiting removal of cattle from the Territory
rubrics_metrics.description: The law prohibits cattle from being removed from the Territory, under heavy penalty. While it is not enforced it prevents the department from issuing license to responsible cattle dealers and irresponsible parties from the States overrun the Territory to the detriment of the Indians. The law should be repealed at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider repealing or revising the prohibition to enable licensing of responsible dealers and reduce predatory, unlicensed droving that harms Indian interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and process claims to tribal citizenship under department rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 531 families ... who claim to be Cherokees and who have applied to the Cherokee citizenship court for confirmation of title and have been rejected. ... Under instructions from the Hon. Commissioner of Indian Affairs, I investigate the claims of these parties, and if I am satisfied they have prima facie a just claim to citizenship, I permit them to remain to await final action in these cases, which is to be determined by rules adopted by the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow departmental rules to investigate prima facie claims to tribal citizenship, allow claimants to remain pending final determination, and expedite rule-based resolution to avoid prolonged detriment to claimants and tribal administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt state school systems and English-only instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The schools of these nations are conducted upon the school system of the States. The English language is taught exclusively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model reservation schools on State systems and emphasize English instruction to integrate students and provide standard educational structures; support teacher pay and school maintenance accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate police and military action against outlaws
rubrics_metrics.description: The frequent visits of soldiers to this agency in search of invaders and outlaws has been the means of preventing much lawlessness, and the breaking up of bands of desperadoes that made this their headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coordinated military patrols and police action where necessary to dismantle organized outlaw bands and secure agency territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define status and legal protections for former slaves (negro population) in tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the Choctaws there are more than 3,000 negroes, who were their former slaves, and whom the government stipulated, in the treaty of 1866, to remove and provide for. Nothing has been done ... The Baptist Home Mission Board ... contribute considerably to make the schools as good as possible, but there are many neighborhoods destitute of schools. Some measures should be adopted to define the status of these people, so that the Indian, as well as the negro, could have the benefit of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify legal/status rights and provide educational and legal protections for former slaves residing within tribes so they receive lawful benefits and services; adopt measures to address neglected neighborhoods and schooling.
